finding_1_browser_flags.key_finding: patchright and nodriver both clear navigator.webdriver, but NEITHER removes the 'HeadlessChrome' UA substring by default. Only an explicit user_agent does.
finding_1_browser_flags.non_discriminating: plugins=5, languages=2, window.chrome=object and the WebGL vendor are identical across all headless runs because all drive the same Chrome binary; they do not separate the tools.

finding_2_tls_stability.method: each impersonation profile probed 3 consecutive times; unique-value counts recorded
finding_2_tls_stability.correction: An earlier draft of this report listed a single JA3 per Chrome profile as a fixture. It was one run's value. Four separate runs produced four different Chrome JA3 sets while Safari and Firefox returned byte-identical JA3 every time.
consequences: a JA3 allowlist cannot reliably pin a Chrome impersonation - the value moves per connection; a JA4 allowlist can
JA4 does not separate adjacent Chrome versions: chrome124 and chrome131 share t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_02713d6af862 while chrome differs
HTTP/2 separates browser families, not versions - all three Chrome profiles emit one hash; Safari and Firefox each emit their own

caveats: single machine, single egress IP; cross-IP fingerprint stability untested, only run-to-run
no real Cloudflare/Akamai challenge attempted, by design
nodriver leaves a closed event loop on teardown; probe.py tolerates it because measurements are collected before teardown
